subject: Literature
title: Cormac McCarthy's The Road
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cormac McCarthy's The Road.

hook.text: The Road is a novel so bleak that Cormac McCarthy said the idea came to him while watching his sleeping son.

buildup.text: A father and son walk through a dead world covered in ash, pushing a shopping cart holding everything they own.

discovery.text: McCarthy never explains what destroyed civilization. The cause does not matter. Only survival and love remain.

twist.text: The novel strips away every comfort of civilization to ask one question: what is worth preserving when everything is gone?

climax.text: The Road argues that even in the worst possible world, the bond between parent and child carries meaning forward.

punchline.text: In the end, love was the only thing that survived.

quiz.question: Why does McCarthy never explain what destroyed civilization?
options: He planned to reveal it in a sequel
The cause does not matter — only survival and love remain
He wanted readers to research and decide for themselves
